A hardware privacy display uses special display layers that physically narrow the viewing angle. It needs display hardware support.\n\nSoftware privacy, like this app, uses overlays, masking and optional face detection. It makes the screen harder to read from the side, but it cannot change how your display emits light.

Privacy Display stores only its own settings, on this device. It never uploads camera frames, never saves face images, does not recognise who you are, and never reads your contacts, messages, passwords or screen contents.
Privacy Mode turns off by itself while one of these apps is open, and turns back on when you leave it.

A phone screen shows the same picture in every direction, so an app cannot make it look blurry only to people at an angle. Instead, the front camera watches for other faces to your left, right, above or below, and blurs the whole screen while they are looking. Nothing is recorded.
